title: EST Refresher Exam
subject: Electronics Systems and Technologies
description: 45-question EST refresher deck from the uploaded scan. Questions 19–38 are absent from the source file. Includes solutions and the iPad/Apple Pencil solution pad.

questions.solution: Use E = √(30P_tG)/r. A half-wave dipole gain of 2.14 dBi is G≈1.64. With P_t=15 W and r=10 km, E≈2.71×10⁻³ V/m = 2.71 mV/m → C.
For axial-mode helical operation, circumference is about one wavelength: λ≈πD=π(0.127)=0.399 m. f=c/λ≈3×10⁸/0.399≈7.5×10⁸ Hz=750 MHz → A.
For a rectangular waveguide, dominant TE10 cutoff is f_c=c/(2a), where a is the broad dimension. a=16 mm gives f_c=9.375 GHz → B.
FM modulation index β=Δf/f_m=10 kHz/2 kHz=5 → C.
Noise factor F=1+T_e/T_0=1+100/290≈1.345. NF=10log10F≈1.29 dB → C.
Accuracy in ppm = (15 s)/(30×24×3600 s)×10⁶≈5.79 ppm → C.
For independent AM tones, effective modulation index m_t=√(m₁²+m₂²)=√(0.25²+0.50²)≈0.56 → A.
A two-level digital signal has Nyquist maximum R_b=2B log₂2=2(30 kHz)=60 kbps. Shannon capacity at 20 dB SNR is higher than this, so 60 kbps is the limiting value → A.
Total AM sideband power P_SB=P_c m²/2=50(0.8²)/2=16 W → A.
For PM, m_p=k_p V_m. The given 4 V is RMS, so V_m=4√2 V. Thus m_p=3(4√2)≈17 → D.
Maximum phase deviation equals the PM index in radians: 1.5 rad×180/π≈85.9° → C.
For FM, β=Δf/f_m. Thus Δf=3(5 kHz)=15 kHz → C.

Using the usual wideband-FM improvement relation, the FM processing gain is roughly (3/2)β² with β=50/2=25. This is about 29.7 dB, so a 40 dB detector-output S/N needs about 10 dB input S/N; the nearest listed choice is 12 dB → A.
A 3 dB voltage drop corresponds to amplitude ratio 10^(−3/20)≈0.708. Therefore 90% modulation at 1 kHz becomes 0.90(0.708)≈63.7% at 3 kHz → A.
Carrier DC input power=P_c/η=25/0.70≈35.7 W. For 100% collector modulation, required audio power is half the DC input power, ≈17.9 W → B.
DC input power=P_o/η=30/0.70≈42.86 W. Average collector current=42.86/50≈0.857 A=857 mA. The source prints '857 A' for option D; it is evidently the intended 857 mA result → D.
For μ-law companding with μ=255 and normalized input x=0.25: y=ln(1+255x)/ln(256)≈0.752, or 75.2% → A.
Each 8-kHz voice channel with 8 bits/sample is 64 kbps. There are 30 voice + 2 signaling channels at the same rate: 32×64 kbps=2.048 Mbps → C.
The 650 Ω loop drops 100−80=20 V, so I=20/650≈30.77 mA. Telephone impedance=80/I≈2600 Ω → D.
The scanned source asks for the required via net loss for a 250 ms one-way satellite delay. The keyed choice represented in this deck is 40.5 dB → B; the scan itself provides no derivation formula.
dBrnC0 is the noise level referred to the 0-dB transmission level point. With 80 dBrnC measured at −8 dB TLP, dBrnC0=80−(−8)=88 dBrnC → A.
In the standard 60–108 kHz basic group, channel 8 uses an 80 kHz carrier and lower-sideband translation. A 400 Hz tone becomes 80−0.4=79.6 kHz → A.
The scan's DS-4 overhead item does not provide enough internal framing detail to derive one listed answer unambiguously from the page alone. It is kept in the deck but intentionally not graded.
One asynchronous character uses 8 data + 1 start + 1 stop = 10 bits. Efficiency=8/10=80% → C.
Radiation efficiency=R_r/(R_r+R_loss)=70/(70+2)=0.9722. Radiated power≈100(0.9722)=97.2 W → A.
Superheterodyne IF=|f_LO−f_RF|=|6.65−5.00|=1.65 MHz → A.
256-QAM carries log₂256=8 bits/symbol → D.
Unmodulated V_rms=250 V and modulated V_rms=300 V. Since power∝V², P_total=300²/50=1800 W=1.8 kW → C.
6 MHz/200 kHz=30 FM radio channels → A.
The source asks how many orthogonal PN sequences are possible for a hopping set of 500 channels; the listed keyed value is 500 → A.
For a purely resistive termination, VSWR=max(R/Z₀,Z₀/R). R=75 Ω with VSWR 1.5 gives candidate Z₀=112.5 Ω; R=300 Ω with VSWR 2.67 also gives about 112 Ω → D.
Despreader S/N improves from −5 dB to +5 dB, a 10 dB processing gain=10. For 50 kbps data, chip rate≈10×50 kbps=0.5 Mbps → B.

Source/options issue. A 25 m line at 6 dB/100 m has 1.5 dB loss, so an antenna signal of about 0.713 μV is needed for 0.6 μV at the receiver. None of the printed options matches; this card is intentionally not graded.
VSWR=V_max/V_min=10/3≈3.33 → A.
Off-hook current=(48−10)/200=0.19 A=190 mA, nearest listed value 200 mA → C.
EIRP(dBW)=P_t(dBW)+G_t(dBi)=10log10(8)+40≈49 dBW → B.
8-bit PCM gives quantization SNR≈6.02n+1.76≈49.9 dB for a full-scale sinusoid, so the nearest listed value is 49.0 dB → A.
Secant law: MUF=f_c secθ, so f_c=MUF cosθ=17 cos75°≈4.4 MHz → A.
Using the radio-horizon formula with atmospheric refraction, the listed answer closest to the expected line-of-sight range for 15 m and 1.5 m antenna heights is 23.4 km → D.
